title: After Hunayn
subtitle: The Spoils of Ji'ranah, the Hawazin Delegation, and the Immortal Tears of the Ansar
summary: Following the decisive triumph at Hunayn, the vast spoils and captives were assembled at Ji'ranah while a brief siege was laid to the fortress of Ta'if. Upon the arrival of a repentant Hawazin delegation, the Prophet facilitated the unconditional return of all their captive women and children through voluntary generosity. In distributing the material spoils to reconcile the hearts of tribal chieftains, the Prophet addressed the initial heartache of the Ansar with an immortal discourse that moved them to copious tears.

sections.text: The Encampment at Ji'ranah and the Siege of Ta'if

Following the route of Hawazin at Wadi Hunayn, their defeated chieftain Malik ibn Awf and surviving warriors fled to the nearby fortified city of Ta'if, barring the massive iron gates of its citadels behind them. The Prophet ordered the vast spoils of Hunayn—consisting of twenty-four thousand camels, forty thousand sheep, and four thousand ounces of silver, alongside six thousand captive women and children—to be safely escorted and secured under guard at the oasis of Al-Ji'ranah.

The Prophet then advanced toward Ta'if, maintaining a disciplined siege around its formidable walls for approximately twenty days. When the defenders deployed heavy catapults and spiked caltrops, inflicting casualties without capitulating, the Prophet consulted his companions. Salman al-Farsi and Nawfal ibn Mu'awiyah advised that Ta'if was like a fox in its burrow; if left alone, it could do no harm. Realizing that the military power of pagan Arabia was already broken and that guidance was imminent, the Prophet lifted the siege, supplicating: 'O Allah, guide the people of Thaqif and bring them to us as Muslims!'
The Hawazin Delegation and the Return of the Captives

Returning to the staging grounds of Al-Ji'ranah, the Prophet delayed the division of spoils for over ten days, hoping that Hawazin would come forward in repentance. His prophetic anticipation was rewarded when a delegation of fourteen chieftains from Hawazin arrived, led by Zuhayr ibn Surad, announcing their collective acceptance of Islam and pleading for the release of their families.

Addressing the assembly, Zuhayr pleaded: 'O Messenger of Allah! Among these captive women are your foster mothers and aunts who nursed you in your childhood among Banu Sa'd!' Deeply moved by their appeal to his childhood bonds with Halimah al-Sa'diyyah, the Prophet stood before his army and announced: 'As for what belongs to me and the children of Abdul-Muttalib, it is freely given to you for the sake of Allah!' Inspired by this supreme example of magnanimity, the Muhajirun and Ansar stood up and proclaimed with one voice: 'What belongs to us is likewise given to the Messenger of Allah!' All six thousand captives were returned unconditionally to their families without ransom, dissolving all remaining enmity into profound love for Islam.

When the remaining livestock and silver were distributed, the Prophet utilized the wealth to cement the political and spiritual unity of Arabia. In accordance with divine legislation concerning those whose hearts are to be reconciled (Mu'allafat Qulubuhum), the Prophet bestowed extraordinarily generous gifts upon prominent Makkan chieftains and bedouin tribal leaders who were new to the faith. Leaders such as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, Safwan ibn Umayyah, Uyaynah ibn Hisn, and Al-Aqra' ibn Habis were each granted one hundred camels and large quantities of silver.

These gifts succeeded remarkably in purifying their hearts from lingering arrogance. Safwan ibn Umayyah later testified: 'By Allah, the Messenger of Allah gave to me when he was the most hated of people to me, and he continued giving to me until he became the most beloved of all people to my heart.'
The Grief of the Ansar and the Prophetic Address

Observing that the vast herds of camels and sheep were being distributed entirely to the recent Makkan converts and desert chieftains, while the Ansar—who had sacrificed their lives, homes, and wealth to shelter Islam—received no material gifts, a sense of quiet sorrow arose among some of the younger men of Madinah. Words circulated among them: 'By Allah, the Messenger of Allah has encountered his own people; his swords still drip with our blood, yet our spoils are given to them!'

When Sa'd ibn Ubadah, the chieftain of the Ansar, informed the Prophet of their feelings, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered all the Ansar to assemble exclusively within a leather pavilion at Ji'ranah, permitting no outsider to enter with them. When they were seated, the Prophet stood before them and delivered an immortal discourse documented in Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim that touched the absolute depths of human devotion:

يَا مَعْشَرَ الأَنْصَارِ! أَلَمْ آتِكُمْ ضُلاَّلاً فَهَدَاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِي؟ وَكُنْتُمْ مُتَفَرِّقِينَ فَأَلَّفَكُمُ اللَّهُ بِي؟ وَعَالَةً فَأَغْنَاكُمُ اللَّهُ بِي؟
'O assembly of the Ansar! Did I not come to you when you were astray and Allah guided you through me? And you were divided and Allah united you through me? And you were impoverished and Allah enriched you through me?' (Sahih al-Bukhari 4330; Sahih Muslim 1059)

At every question, the Ansar lowered their heads in humility and answered: 'Allah and His Messenger are most bountiful and gracious!' The Prophet continued: 'Why do you not answer me, O Ansar? If you wished, you could say with absolute truth: 'You came to us rejected and we believed in you; you came to us abandoned and we sheltered you; you came to us impoverished and we comforted you!' Have you found grief in your hearts, O Ansar, over a trifling bit of worldly goods with which I reconciled the hearts of a people that they might accept Islam, while I entrusted you to your firm faith?'
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ looked upon them with tears in his eyes and delivered the crowning words that sealed their eternal honor:

أَمَا تَرْضَوْنَ يَا مَعْشَرَ الأَنْصَارِ أَنْ يَذْهَبَ النَّاسُ بِالشَّاةِ وَالْبَعِيرِ، وَتَرْجِعُونَ بِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ إِلَى رِحَالِكُمْ؟ فَوَالَّذِي نَفْسِي بِيَدِهِ، لَوْلاَ الْهِجْرَةُ لَكُنْتُ امْرَأً مِنَ الأَنْصَارِ... اللَّهُمَّ ارْحَمِ الأَنْصَارَ، وَأَبْنَاءَ الأَنْصَارِ، وَأَبْنَاءَ أَبْنَاءِ الأَنْصَارِ
'Are you not pleased, O Ansar, that people depart with sheep and camels, while you return with the Messenger of Allah to your homes? By Him in whose hand is my soul! Were it not for the Hijrah, I would have been a man of the Ansar! O Allah, have mercy upon the Ansar, and the children of the Ansar, and the grandchildren of the Ansar!' (Sahih al-Bukhari 4330; Sahih Muslim 1059)

The pavilion erupted into uncontrollable weeping. The Ansar wept until their beards were completely soaked with tears, crying out from the depths of their souls: 'We are well-pleased with the Messenger of Allah as our portion and our share!'

Following the profound reconciliation at Ji'ranah, the Prophet performed Umrah from that blessed sanctuary before returning in triumph to Madinah. The campaigns of Khaybar, Makkah, and Hunayn were successfully completed, establishing undisputed stability across western Arabia and setting the stage for the universal delegation year and the final stages of the prophetic mission.
